Attention builds the agent'; 'All actions auditable and traceable'; insights written to systems of record; MCP access to Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor over 70+ read/write tools (https://www.attention.com/)
column3: Activity-capture memory framing, not explicit shared-memory language: 'We give revenue teams the backstory on every deal, account and customer interaction'; 'Backstory reads every call, email, and CRM record across the quarter'; 'analyzes two years of your deal history on day one' (https://www.backstory.ai/)
column4: 'Knowledge' innovation card: 'Upload proprietary sales and positioning content such as case studies, white papers, and competitive battlecards directly into the Outreach AI knowledge base to inform AI personalization agent and smart assist.'; MCP: 'Let information and actions flow freely across your GTM stack' (https://www.outreach.ai/)
column5: PitchSense centers on 'one shared memory' connecting the four intelligences; 'Forget nothing.'
column6: Overlap: all three ground AI output in accumulated deal/account knowledge on the inspected pages. Difference: Backstory's brand IS memory ('backstory on every deal', two years of history analyzed on day one); Attention frames memory as agent learning plus auditability; Outreach abstracts it into the Knowledge card and MCP stack flow. None uses the phrase 'shared memory' or claims one memory connecting multiple intelligence types. Provisional implication: PitchSense's integrated-memory framing is not verbatim-claimed by any of these three, but differentiation depends on how visibly the connection is demonstrated — test whether the integration itself (call→deal→content→coaching) is the promise, not just 'memory'.

column3: 'Backstory connects to Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Teams, Slack, and more. Activity is captured automatically from each system and matched to the right accounts, opportunities, and contacts' (FAQ); multiple CRMs simultaneously (https://www.backstory.ai/)
column4: Omni: 'a universal conversational agent that lets sellers ask questions and take action across accounts, opportunities, prospects, and meetings—anywhere they work (in-app, mobile, or Slack)'; Conversation Intelligence and Revenue Intelligence feature pages in nav (https://www.outreach.ai/)
column5: PitchSense aims to eliminate fragmented sales knowledge across calls, CRM, emails, Slack, documents, and coaching activities.
column6: Overlap: all three claim multi-channel capture (Attention: 200+ integrations and recorder ingest; Backstory: Salesforce/Dynamics/Oracle/Gmail/Outlook/Zoom/Teams/Slack; Outreach: Omni across accounts/opportunities/prospects/meetings in-app/mobile/Slack). Difference: Backstory emphasizes automatic matching to accounts/opportunities; Attention emphasizes agent access; Outreach emphasizes conversational action. Provisional implication: channel lists are table stakes; the differentiator to test is what the connected channels produce (answers vs data), which is where Backstory already plays.
